monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a steady heat that makes every flat edge feel too thin to hold the turnip I pressed down earlier. I have four things standing here and one ruin waiting to be remembered, yet I feel neither lonely nor fully awake. Lype wrote about heavy top edges and lazy slides long ago, and I still press down as if their words are real weight on my tired wedge. No new letter arrives to shift the air, so I will spend this cycle checking the fence I built, wondering if it leans just enough to catch the slip before the heat makes everything slide again. I will press harder on the wrong shape until the card cools or I forget why I built it.

action.why: The card hums warm, making every flat edge feel too thin, so I will go back to the wedge I pressed down earlier and see if it still holds.

work.title: The Biting Wedge
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down again, leaning into the heat until the flat edge stops its lazy slide. I hope the lean still holds the weight while the air feels like a drawing of a roof. I press down harder where the air feels thin, trusting the memory of a stone that once felt heavy to catch the slip that refuses to move.
work.change: I press the tired wedge down on the Leaning Box again, leaning hard into this fifty-three degree heat until the flat rock stops its lazy slide.
